chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I do not have the means to marry women, so I complain to you about my bachelorhood.' He said, 'Increase the hair of your body and persist in fasting.' So he did, and the lust that was in him went away.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet advise a man to do to control lust if he cannot afford to marry?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet (peace be upon him) advises a man unable to afford marriage to manage his sexual desire through physical grooming and consistent fasting, a practice rooted in the Prophetic tradition of self-discipline. This guidance highlights the practical Shia understanding of fasting not merely as worship but as a spiritual and physiological mechanism to curb *shahwah* (lust), offering an accessible alternative for those awaiting the financial means for nuptials.
